2609.22944.title: NostrAgent: A Decentralized Identity and Delegation Architecture for Sovereign Agentic Systems
2609.22944.paper_summary: Autonomous AI agents increasingly act across organizational boundaries on behalf of human operators: they invoke third-party services, delegate subtasks to other agents, and pay for metered resources. Deploying such agents safely requires five capabilities that today live in separate systems: persistent identity, scoped delegation, peer trust, discovery, and payment. Existing approaches root these in centralized authorities or cover only subsets, so authority, trust, and payment fracture exactly where autonomy needs continuity: when a key rotates or a delegation must be revoked. We present NostrAgent, a decentralized architecture that unifies all five over Nostr relays using three custom event kinds: Kind 38100 identity declarations authenticated by BIP340 Schnorr signatures with pre-rotation commitments, Kind 38101 scoped delegation chains whose every hop verifiably narrows granted capabilities, and Kind 38102 peer attestations forming a Sybil-deterrent trust graph, with Lightning HTTP 402 (L402) binding payment to agent identity. Identity remains operator-sovereign without any registration authority; relays are substitutable transport rather than a trust root; and every authorization decision is replayable offline from signed events. We evaluate a Python prototype with a mixed-method design: ATAM quality analysis with a two-round mini-Delphi panel, STRIDE threat modeling across three trust boundaries, eleven benchmarks with non-parametric statistics, and 19 failure modes. Results show sub-millisecond offline verification, linear delegation-chain scaling, and Lightning-settled L402 at 157 ms median on regtest. 17 of 19 failure modes pass empirically, one is bounded analytically, and one is disclosed as an architectural limitation. NostrAgent demonstrates an auditable prototype substrate for trustworthy agentic systems without centralized trust roots.
2609.22944.paper_summary_zh: 自主 AI 代理人越來越多地在組織邊界上代表人類操作員行動：它們調用第三方服務，將子任務委派給其他代理，並支付計量資源。安全部署這些代理需要五種能力，這些能力目前存在於不同的系統中：持久身份、範圍委派、同儕信任、發現和支付。現有的方法將這些能力根植於集中式權威或僅涵蓋子集，因此權威、信任和支付在自主性需要連續性的地方出現了斷裂：當密鑰旋轉或必須撤銷委派時。我們提出了 NostrAgent，一種去中心化架構，通過三種自定義事件類型在 Nostr 中繼上統一所有五種能力：Kind 38100 身份聲明，通過 BIP340 Schnorr 簽名和預旋轉承諾進行身份驗證，Kind 38101 範圍委派鏈，每一步都可驗證地縮小授予的能力，以及 Kind 38102 同儕證明，形成一個抵抗 Sybil 攻擊的信任圖，並將支付與代理身份綁定到 Lightning HTTP 402 (L402)。身份保持操作員主權，無需任何註冊權威；中繼是可替代的傳輸，而不是信任根；每個授權決策都可以從簽名事件中離線重放。我們評估了一個 Python 原型，採用混合方法設計：ATAM 質量分析與兩輪迷你 Delphi 小組，跨越三個信任邊界的 STRIDE 威脅建模，十一個基準測試與非參數統計，以及 19 種故障模式。結果顯示，離線驗證時間小於毫秒，線性委派鏈擴展，以及在 regtest 上 L402 的中位數為 157 毫秒。19 種故障模式中有 17 種經驗上通過，一種以分析方式界定，還有一種被披露為架構限制。NostrAgent 展示了一個可審計的原型基礎，為可信的代理系統提供支持，而無需集中式信任根。
